name: Li Ka-shing
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Nicknamed Superman, Li Ka-shing is revered as one of the most influential businessmen in Asia.
Li retired as chairman of CK Hutchison Holdings and CK Asset Holdings in 2018 but remains senior advisor.
His son Victor now heads the conglomerate, which has more than 300,000 employees and operates in more than 50 nations.
Li started Cheung Kong Plastics, named after the Yangtze River, in 1950 at age 21 with $6,500 in savings and loans from relatives.
His Li Ka Shing Foundation has donated more than $3.8 billion; over 80% has gone to Greater China.
forbes_facts: Li says it took him five minutes in 2007 to decide to invest in Facebook, even though it barely had any revenues. He also invested in Siri and Spotify.
At age 12, Li fled China with his family. Two years later his father, who had been a primary school principal in China but then worked at a watch factory, died.
At the announcement of his retirement, Li joked that he'd been "working for a long time, too long."

name: François Pinault
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1997-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: François Pinault is honorary chairman of luxury group Kering, which owns fashion brands Saint Laurent, Alexander McQueen and Gucci.
Pinault founded Kering, which started as a wood and building materials company, in 1963.
In 1999, Pinault changed the direction of the business toward luxury goods when he bought a controlling stake in Gucci Group.
Today the $17.2 billion (2025 sales) company, which also owns Balenciaga and Saint Laurent, is run by Pinault's son, François-Henri.
Pinault and his family own iconic auction house Christie's, plus a 3,000-piece art collection with works by Picasso, Mondrian and Koons.
In 2023, they bought a majority stake in talent agency Creative Artists Agency from private-equity firm TPG.
forbes_facts: Pinault and his family also own several vineyards, a French soccer club, a theater in Paris and a luxury yacht and expedition company.
The Pinault family gave more than $100 million to help rebuild the Notre Dame Cathedral following the 2019 fire.

name: Richard Tsai
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025)
forbes_bio: With billionaire brother Daniel, Richard Tsai leads Fubon Financial Holding, a family company with interests in banking, insurance and securities.
The brothers are investors in Taiwan Mobile, a mobile phone service provider, and Momo, a TV-shopping and ecommerce business.
They also own a stake in Diamond Biofund, a Taipei-based biotech venture capital firm that went public in 2023.
Cousins Tsai Hong-tu, Tsai Cheng-da and T.Y. Tsai are also billionaires.

name: Leonard Stern
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Leonard Stern joined his father Max's pet supply business in 1959. Seven years later he expanded into real estate, acquiring a New Jersey warehouse.
His Hartz Mountain firm owns more than 260 real estate properties, mostly in the New Jersey area.
Most of Hartz's portfolio is in warehouses, including properties in New Jersey, Atlanta, Baltimore and Charlotte, N.C.
Stern sold the pet business for $350 million in 2000. He has also ventured into publishing, energy, capital management and carpet cleaning.
Many know his name thanks to his $30 million donation 30 years ago to New York University's business school, renamed in his honor.
forbes_facts: Leonard's father Max Stern arrived in New York from Germany in 1926 with 5,000 canaries -- a friend's way to repay a loan.
In 2015, Stern's son Eddie was named Hartz's president and chief operating officer. He will eventually succeed his father as chairman and CEO.

name: Du Shuanghua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2010-2022); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026)
forbes_bio: Du Shaunghua chairs Rizhao Steel Holding Group.
Rizhao Steel Holding is one of China's largest private steel manufacturers.
Du is a philanthropist whose donations have supported youth causes.

name: Dona Bertarelli
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: The bulk of Dona Bertarelli's wealth comes from the 2007 sale of her family's biotech business Serono for over $13 billion.
In the 1990s Dona was Serono's executive director of public and professional affairs.
Her brother Ernesto is the richest man in Switzerland. They split ownership of most family assets.
She now focuses her time on marine conservation efforts and is a special adviser to the United Nations.
forbes_facts: Bertarelli became the fastest woman to sail around the world when her team raced for the Jules Verne Trophy in 2016.
She owns the Park Gstaad hotel, Five Seas Hotel in Cannes and Country Club Geneva.

name: Andrei Skoch
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Andrei Skoch is a partner in Russian investment group, USM, and has been a member of the State Duma, Russia's legislative body, since 1999.
He and his former partner, Lev Kvetnoi, were born in a settlement near Moscow and studied at the same athletics school, Institute of Physical Culture.
The partners merged their business with that of billionaire Alisher Usmanov. Kvetnoi later sold out.
As a member of the Duma, he isn't allowed to own stakes in businesses so his shares in USM are held by his father Vladimir and his daughter Varvara.
Skoch was sanctioned by the U.S. in 2018 for "longstanding ties to Russian organized criminal groups," which he has denied. The EU and U.K. sanctioned him in 2022.
forbes_facts: He built a memorial to fallen Russian soldiers in Lushun, China, formerly known as Port Arthur, the site of the bloodiest battles of the 1904-05 Russo-Japanese War.

name: Mathias Boehringer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Mathias Boehringer owes his fortune to pharma giant Boehringer Ingelheim, the largest private player in the pharmaceutical industry.
Founded in 1885 by Albert Boehringer with 28 employees, the company got its start by making ingredients for pharmacies, textile merchants and the food industry.
Today Boehringer Ingelheim employs 53,000 people and has a presence in 130 markets.
Mathias along with 14 members of the family -- all in the third, fourth or fifth generation -- own equal parts of the company.

name: Alexander Abramov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Alexander Abramov was chairman of steel company Evraz, which is also his biggest holding, until March 2022. He resigned after his partner Roman Abramovich was hit by UK sanctions.
Abramov himself was hit with UK sanctions in November 2022. He has been under sanctions in New Zealand (where he has property) since 2009.
Abramov got his start as the head of a research lab before the collapse of the Soviet Union.
In 1992, he founded a precursor to Evraz Holding and made a fortune exporting metals and coal from the Urals and Siberia.
After the 1998 Russian financial crisis, he bought up hobbled steel companies on the cheap, including two U.S. firms, Claymont Steel and Oregon Steel.
In 2017, Russian President Vladimir Putin awarded Abramov the Decoration For Beneficence for his public work and charity activity.

name: Marc Stad
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Marc Stad founded Dragoneer Investment Group, a $37 billion (assets under management) venture capital firm focused on technology investments.
Stad began his career in public service as president and commissioner of the City and County of San Francisco Finance Corporation, helping oversee financial assistance to the city and county.
He then moved into finance with stints at McKinsey, TPG and the Investment Group of Santa Barbara.
He launched Dragoneer in 2012. It has invested in giants in the technology industry, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Spotify and Uber.

Stad and his wife pledged $3 million to the University of California, San Francisco's UCSF Benioff Children's Hospitals in 2022 to launch the Stad Center for Pediatric Pain to treat children with acute pain.
In August 2026, Stad stuck a deal to become the controlling owner of the NBA's Minnesota Timberwolves and the WNBA's Minnesota Lynx.

name: Masahiro Noda
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2000-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Masahiro Noda is the chairman and CEO of publicly traded computer-system integrator and custom software maker Obic.
Obic is known for its accounting software and its television ads featuring a Kabuki actor.
In the fiscal year through March 2025, the company posted $452 million in net profit on $848 million in revenue.
Noda launched the business with his wife's savings in 1968.

name: Daniel Sundheim
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Daniel Sundheim is chief investment officer of hedge fund D1 Capital Partners, which he founded in 2018.
The firm has around $31 billion in assets under management, with the majority invested in private companies, including a large SpaceX stake.
D1 Capital's public and private portfolios both returned more than 30% in 2025, reaching new highs to recover from losses in 2021 and 2022.
Sundheim graduated from the University of Pennsylvania and spent 15 years working under billionaire Andreas Halvorsen at Viking Global Investors.
